sections.h2: Connecticut landlord and tenant laws by chapter
sections.html:
Most landlord and tenant rules live in Title 47a of the General Statutes, split into chapters by subject. A landlord preparing to sell a rental will touch several of them, so it helps to know which chapter answers which question.

ChapterSubject
830Rights and responsibilities of landlord and tenant
831Security deposits
832Summary process (eviction)
833Entry and detainer
833aPublic enforcement of health and safety standards in rented dwellings

The Judicial Branch law library keeps a landlord and tenant page with links to these chapters, to forms, and to research reports from the Office of Legislative Research. Treat it as a place to start research, not as legal advice.

sections.h2: What a landlord must keep in working order
sections.html:
Under section 47a-7, a landlord has to follow the building and housing codes that affect health and safety and keep the premises fit and habitable. The duty has exceptions when the tenant or a guest made the place unfit on purpose. The statute spells out the day-to-day tasks.

  • Make repairs and do whatever is needed to keep the premises fit and habitable.
  • Keep the common areas clean and safe.
  • Keep electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating and ventilating systems, appliances and elevators that the landlord supplies or must supply in good and safe working order.
  • Provide and maintain containers for ashes, garbage and other waste.

These duties follow the house. A buyer who steps into the landlord's role inherits them, and an inspection that turns up tired heating or plumbing in a rented unit can pull an offer down. Investors buying as-is usually price that risk in instead of asking for repairs.

Rent is not late for nine days after the due date, or four days on a one-week tenancy. Only once that grace period ends may a landlord terminate for nonpayment under sections 47a-23 to 47a-23b. The grace rule is section 47a-15a.

A valid written late-charge agreement in the lease lets the landlord charge a fee on a payment made after the grace period. The fee cannot exceed the lesser of five dollars a day, up to fifty dollars, or five percent of the late payment. When a government or charitable entity covers part of the rent, the five percent applies to the tenant's share only. One late payment can carry only one late fee, however long it stays open.

A buyer will want a rent roll and payment history. Clean records of due dates, grace periods and fees head off questions at the closing table.

sections.h2: Showing a rented home to buyers
sections.html:
A landlord can show a rental, within limits. Section 47a-16 says a tenant may not unreasonably refuse consent for the landlord to enter to show the unit to prospective or actual purchasers, in addition to entering to inspect or make repairs.

The tenant's privacy stays protected. Without consent, a landlord may enter only in an emergency (section 47a-16a), under a court order, or when the tenant has abandoned the premises. Entry cannot be abused or used to harass, and it must happen at reasonable times except in an emergency.

Showings go better when planned with the tenant. Set windows and a short list of expected visitors beat a string of last-minute requests. A cash buyer who wants to see a tenant-occupied house can often manage one visit instead of a run of open houses.

sections.h2: Security deposits when the landlord sells
sections.html:
The deposit goes to the new owner. Section 47a-21 treats any voluntary or involuntary transfer of the landlord's interest in residential property as an assignment to the successor of the landlord's security interest in every deposit the tenants paid.

The seller has to move the money. On a transfer from a landlord, other than a receiver, the landlord must withdraw the full deposits plus accrued interest from the escrow account and deliver them to the successor. Where the account also holds deposits for other properties and has less than the total, the seller delivers a pro rata share for the property being sold. A successor includes anyone who gets the landlord's interest by purchase, foreclosure or otherwise.

  • Return deadline: no later than twenty-one days after the tenancy ends, or fifteen days after the tenant gives a written forwarding address, whichever is later.
  • Amount returned: the full deposit plus accrued interest, less any damage deductions the landlord may take.

Section 47a-6 requires a landlord, or a successor landlord, to tell the tenant in writing at the time of succession the name and address of the person authorized to manage the premises. The statute names a second person too, so read the full text.

The Department of Housing posts mandatory landlord and tenant notice forms on its website, and the Judicial Branch page links to them. A buyer taking over a rental should bring the notice to closing, along with lease copies, the deposit transfer and any records of repairs or complaints.

Tenants take a sale better when they hear about it from the owner. One short written note naming the seller, the buyer and the new contact cuts confusion and missed rent.

sections.h2: Tenants with extra protection from eviction
sections.html:
Section 47a-23c limits evictions of older and disabled tenants in larger properties. It reaches a tenant who is 62 or older or has a qualifying disability and lives in a building or complex of five or more dwelling units, or in a mobile manufactured home park. Some tenants who live with a relative meeting those conditions are covered as well.

A landlord can sue such a tenant only on the listed grounds, and a rent increase must be fair and equitable under the criteria in section 7-148c. A protected tenant aggrieved by a proposed increase can go to the town's fair rent commission if there is one, or to Superior Court if there is not. Public Act 22-30, which concerns fair rent commissions, took effect October 1, 2022.

Selling the building is not a listed ground. Buyers of small apartment buildings should ask for each tenant's age and status before agreeing on a price.

Gather the paper trail first. This short list keeps a sale on schedule.

  1. Copy each lease and rental agreement, with rent amounts and dates.
  2. Confirm where each security deposit is held and how much interest has built up.
  3. Write down repair requests and what was done about them under section 47a-7.
  4. Check whether any tenant falls under section 47a-23c.
  5. Decide whether to sell with tenants in place or after they leave, and put any move-out deal in writing.

Landlords with worn-out rentals often sell to a cash investor. The buyer takes the property as-is and deals with the leases after closing, so the owner skips repairs, showings and a lender's approval wait.

sections.h2: Leases and the buyer after closing
sections.html:
A lease does not vanish at closing. Whether it continues depends on its terms and on the notice and court rules, so read it before you set a price and ask an attorney about anything unusual. The buyer becomes the landlord for deposit purposes, takes on the repair duties from section 47a-7, and has to send the written notice about who manages the property.

If the seller and buyer want the unit empty, the only lawful routes are a negotiated move-out agreed in writing or a notice to quit and the court process. A buyer who wants a tenant gone should say so up front, because it changes the price and the closing date.

faqs.q: What is the maximum security deposit in Connecticut?
faqs.a: The cap is two months' rent for a tenant under 62 and one month's rent for a tenant 62 or older under section 47a-21.

faqs.q: How soon must a landlord return a deposit?
faqs.a: A landlord must deliver the deposit with accrued interest, less allowed deductions, no later than 21 days after the tenancy ends or 15 days after a written forwarding address, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Does a new owner have to honor the existing lease?
faqs.a: The chapter treats a successor as a landlord and passes the deposits along. Whether a lease continues depends on its terms and on the notice and court rules, so read the lease and ask an attorney.

faqs.q: Can a landlord enter a rental without notice?
faqs.a: Only in an emergency, under a court order, as permitted by section 47a-16a, or when the unit has been abandoned. Otherwise entry needs the tenant's consent and a reasonable time.

faqs.q: Where can I find Connecticut landlord and tenant forms?
faqs.a: The Judicial Branch law library page for landlord and tenant law links housing forms, and the Department of Housing posts mandatory notice forms and a model lease.
